chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim, the owner of the barley, from Kathir ibn Kaltham, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words'
He said: 'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me, and You are the best of those who forgive.'

'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.'
'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so turn to me in forgiveness, for You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful.'

And in another narration, regarding His Statement, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words,' he said: 'He asked for forgiveness by the right of Muhammad, and Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, and Fatima, peace be upon them.'

key_terms.أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ: the most merciful of the merciful
key_terms.ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي: I have been unjust to myself
key_terms.كَلِماتٍ: words (plural of kalimah, referring to the specific supplication)

ai.seo_question: What were the specific words Adam learned from his Lord for repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the 'Kalimat' (words) Adam received for repentance, presenting three variations that highlight the attributes of Allah as the Forgiver, the Merciful, and the Accepter of Repentance. A significant alternative narration links this primordial act of repentance to the right (Haqq) of the Ahl al-Bayt, underscoring their intercessory role in Shia theology. This connection illustrates how the Prophet and Imams serve as the means through which divine mercy is accessed, a concept deeply rooted in the narrative of human fallibility and redemption.
